extracted.intended_audience: writers, readers, and researchers interested in African short fiction and literary awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and factual criteria related to eligibility and evaluation for the Caine Prize for African Writing, an annual award for the best short story by an African writer published in English. Useful for potential entrants, researchers, and readers wanting to understand what the prize rewards and how entries have been judged or criticised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded for — best short story
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is an annual literary award for the best short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Caine Prize is explicitly awarded for a single short story (the article repeatedly refers to it as a short story prize and lists winning short stories). Entrants and judges treat the unit of work as a short story rather than a novel, essay or other form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility — African writer
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for the best short story by an African writer, whether in Africa or elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize is for 'an African writer' and explicitly includes writers living on the continent or abroad; nationality/identity as an African writer is the core authorship eligibility criterion described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement — English
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must be published in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening line and infobox state the prize is for short stories 'published in the English language', so entrants must have their story available in English (publication in English is a stated requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication status — published work
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is for stories that have been published (the phrasing is 'published in the English language').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article's wording implies entries must be published — the prize is for the best short story 'published in the English language' rather than unpublished manuscripts; exact submission rules (e.g., publication venues or dates) are not specified on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging qualities — powerful language, distinctive tone, bold compelling storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges praise entries for 'powerful language, distinctive tone of voice, and bold, compelling storytelling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phrase appears in coverage of the Best of Caine award (NoViolet Bulawayo) and reflects qualities judges have explicitly commended: linguistic strength, a distinctive authorial voice, and storytelling that takes risks and compels readers. Use as an example of the kind of literary strengths rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging composition — diverse literary professionals with African literature connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges represent a variety of literary fields and include notable authors, artists, journalists, broadcasters and academics with a connection to literature in Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article describes the typical makeup of judging panels; while not a submission requirement, this signals the perspectives and expertise likely applied when evaluating stories (literary, cultural and critical sensibilities connected to African writing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and attribution — must properly attribute sources; plagiarism leads to removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be original and correctly attribute sources; a shortlisted story was removed in 2019 after 'the author's failure to attribute a core source.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2019 incident (removal of a shortlisted story) illustrates that ethical standards around attribution and originality are enforced and that failures can lead to disqualification or removal from shortlists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern — avoid stereotyping Africa to appeal to judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism exists that the prize may incentivize stories that stereotype Africa or 'skew their written perspectives to fit what they imagine will sell to the West and the judges of the Caine Prize.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This critique (quoted from Ikhide Ikheloa) functions as a caution: entries perceived as pandering to Western expectations or recycling predictable, stereotypical portrayals risk being judged negatively by critics and may be viewed as contributing to 'orthodoxy and mediocrity.' Writers should avoid writing to stereotypes or perceived marketable tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize aim — bringing African writing to a wider audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The Caine Prize is a registered charity with the aim of bringing African writing to a wider audience through an annual literary award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a submission constraint, this stated aim implies that works with potential to reach, represent, or resonate with broader readerships and to raise the profile of African writing align with the prize's mission.
